note: The genealogies from Adam to the return, and David's reign retold with attention to worship and the temple. A Tier 6 book, indexed by the Song of Solomon precedent. Not cited by the curriculum or the Scriptural Appendix.
coverage_note: One entry, by design. Chapters 1-9 are genealogies. Chapters 10-29 largely parallel 1-2 Samuel, which are indexed; the parallels are not re-indexed. The lists of officials, Levites, singers and gatekeepers (12, 15-16, 23-27) and the census (21) are not indexed. 4:9-10 (the prayer of Jabez) is not indexed: it is one line in a genealogy, and the index will not lift it out of that setting into a formula for blessing.

entries.pericope: Who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you. For we are strangers before you, and foreigners
entries.connection: The people have given generously for the temple, and David's prayer refuses to let anyone take credit for it, himself included: 'But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.' Habitual Almsgiving with its theology stated — the giver returns what was always God's (medium). C18 and C22. Then C17's self-understanding in the same breath: 'For we are strangers before you, and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow.' And the prayer for the next generation: 'keep this forever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you.'
